description: prHourlyLimit is 0 (unlimited) rather than the default 2: the workflow runs once a week, so a per-hour cap is really a per-week cap and a backlog would drain two PRs at a time. prConcurrentLimit is the gate that is meant to bite.

postUpgradeTasks.description: `pnpm update --changeset` writes a changeset for the bumps its own run makes, and Renovate never makes such a run — it rewrites the range itself. The script reads the change Renovate has already made and hands the writing to `pnpm change`. `update` mode rather than `branch` because only per-upgrade mode exposes the templated fields that say which dep in which manifest moved.

packageRules.description: Never raise a published peer range on a consumer's behalf — bumping the `zod` or `next` floor drops support for versions that worked, which is a breaking change dressed up as a chore. `widen` only ever adds a major to the range. Dev ranges still track latest via the top-level `bump`, so the lockfile stays current either way.
